name: morph-slider
title: Morph Slider
description: A full-width image slider whose slides dissolve through a liquid melt, ripple, shear or swirl effect. Captions cross-fade, arrows step through slides and dots mark the position.
use: A hero or gallery wants a cinematic photo carousel with a stand-out transition and captions.
avoid: The morph is a WebGL shader, so it is heavy on low-end devices and needs a fixed-height, sized parent.
a11y: Captions use a live region and controls are labelled; reduced motion only shortens the morph instead of removing it. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A large rounded rectangle holding a full-bleed landscape photo, framed by a thin black border of empty stage. A dark translucent caption sits at the bottom left, round arrow buttons at mid height and a row of small dots at the bottom centre.
behaves: Slides change with a shader that warps and melts the outgoing photo into the incoming one, briefly smearing colours. Captions fade and lift, the active dot stretches, and autoplay advances after a pause while hovering stops it.
customise: Items, start index, transition mode, duration, easing, intensity, scale, aberration, drift, autoplay and delay, loop, radius, overlay colour, captions, controls and indicators are props.
weight: heavy: A WebGL shader plus a continuous requestAnimationFrame render loop for the drift.
demo: Captions Dolomites at first light, Coastline late afternoon, Desert road golden hour, over mountain and building photos.
issues: Captions do not match the photos shown: the desert-road caption sits over a green alpine valley.
polishWhy: Cinematic slides and clean controls, but the caption and photo mismatch is noticeable.
